I'll look through the notes folder first so the plan matches how the files are named and organized today.Seven minutes files use seven different name styles. Nothing else links to them, so a date-based rename and a short index will tidy the folder without touching the minutes themselves.Seven minutes files in `notes/` will be renamed to `YYYY-MM-DD.md` from each heading date, and `notes/index.md` will list them in order. Minutes text stays as it is.

## File names

| Current name | New name |
| --- | --- |
| `aug11.md` | `2026-08-11.md` |
| `minutes 25 aug.md` | `2026-08-26.md` |
| `Meeting sept 8.md` | `2026-09-08.md` |
| `notes_2026-09-22.md` | `2026-09-22.md` |
| `oct6 meeting notes.md` | `2026-10-06.md` |
| `2026.10.20 minutes.md` | `2026-10-20.md` |
| `Nov 3 (final).md` | `2026-11-03.md` |

`minutes 25 aug.md` is the only date mismatch. The old name uses the cancelled Monday (25 August). The heading says the meeting was held on 26 August after the storm, so the new name follows the heading. The "(final)" tag on 3 November stays out of the filename. Those minutes already say there are no further meetings this year, and the index will say so.

Nothing else in the project links to these filenames, and the folder is not a git repository.

## Index

`notes/index.md` will be a chronological list, oldest first: one link per meeting and a short line on what was decided or still open (noticeboard, shed lights, second tap, roof, fees, gate, compost, work day, winter close). It will note that 26 August was moved from 25 August, and that 3 November is the last meeting of 2026.

The project `README.md` sentence about `notes/` will point at `notes/index.md`. `members.csv` and the minutes text will not change.
